text:
incident-bot: paging: high tail latency + error rate spike on continuous-batching runtime (sev-2). service: inference-runtime, alert: cb_tail_latency_95, current: 2.1s -> 6.8s
Maya P: I'm on it. seeing concurrent queue depth climb and a ton of KV cache evictions in logs.
Alex C: confirming. dashboards: token throughput steady, but request latency distribution is bimodal. increased microbatch assembly time.
Raul G: looks like continuous batching loop is stalling when cache miss storm happens. KV-store eviction logs look like: `evict key prefix=<user:ctx> rate=1200/s` then many subsequent cache repop cycles.
Jess H: any customer-facing errors? support flagged a spike in 504s to a few enterprise customers. CS asking for ETA.
Maya P: impact: ~1% of requests 504, tail latency 95/99 up. affected routes: chat-gen-prod and batch-embed. most visible on high-concurrency nodes (100+ concurrent).
Alex C: quick theory: microbatch size estimator grows with inflight depth. At high concurrency jitter accumulates and KV cache churn causes assembly to block waiting for KV reads.
Raul G: repro snippet from logs: `microbatch_wait start=0.002s end=1.8s reason=kv_miss_fetch` repeated across workers.
Maya P: mitigation options: 1) force microbatch cap to small value (4) 2) enable aggressive KV eviction backpressure to stop repop loops 3) fallback to single-request non-continuous batching on affected nodes.
Jess H: customers need a rollback plan quickly. can we do a config hotfix that rolls out to 3 nodes first?
Alex C: I'll prepare a hotpatch: set CONT_BATCH_MAX_MICROBATCH=4 and CONT_BATCH_JITTER=0.05 for nodes in us-west-prod pool. also enable KV_SLOW_PATH_THROTTLE=1 to rate-limit repop.
ops-bot: suggested command: `kubectl patch configmap runtime-config -n prod -p '{"data":{"CONT_BATCH_MAX_MICROBATCH":"4","CONT_BATCH_JITTER":"0.05","KV_SLOW_PATH_THROTTLE":"1"}}'`
Raul G: please run on a canary subset (3 pods) first, monitor latency and eviction rate.
Maya P: running canary now on node set id=usw-prod-canary-3.
Alex C: rolling patch via deploy pipeline: `deploy-bot apply config canary=usw-prod-canary-3`.
incident-bot: oncall handoff reminder: @Jess H is primary, @Maya P is secondary.
Jess H: I'm coordinating CS comms. letting affected customers know we're mitigating, ETA ~15min for canary results.
Maya P: canary patched. watching metrics: eviction rate dropped ~70% within 45s, 95p latency down from 6.8s -> 1.5s on canary nodes.
Alex C: good sign. if stable for 5m we should escalate to 25% rollout. watch for increased token cost or throughput regression.
Raul G: also enabling a KV-prefetch cooldown to avoid stampede: set KV_PREFETCH_BACKOFF_MS=200. adding to rollout.
Jess H: CS updated: they asked for timeline and recovery steps, sent short note. Customers asked whether any requests lost — confirming we'll follow up once we validate no data loss.
Maya P: after 4m canary looks good, moving to 25% (usw-prod-1..4). patching now.
Alex C: patch completed to 25%. monitoring.
ops-bot: note: watch for increased request queuing on nodes with microbatch cap lowered; set queue_limit=500 to avoid per-node overload.
Raul G: telemetry shows microbatch assembly time stable, KV miss downstream calls reduced, overall latency normalized around 0.9s 95p. error rate back to baseline.
Jess H: CS: telling customers we're seeing recovery and continuing to monitor.
Maya P: plan for next steps: 1) Keep config for 12 hours while we analyze root cause 2) create a revert runbook if we see regression 3) postmortem to dig into estimator algorithm + KV prefetch policy.
Alex C: creating a short hotfix PR to make microbatch cap dynamic by region; will add feature flag for full rollback.
Raul G: follow-up: collect KV eviction traces and a sample of request ids to correlate hot prefixes. I'll take ownership for tracing.
Jess H: oncall summary for ops log: high-concurrency KV repop storm caused continuous-batch stalls -> 95/99 tail latency spike and small customer 504 rate. mitigated via microbatch cap, jitter reduction, KV throttle and prefetch backoff.
incident-bot: incident severity downgraded to sev-3 as user-facing error subsided.
Maya P: thanks team. I'll open the postmortem ticket and link logs + config diffs. cc @Alex C @Raul G for analysis.
